mathematical_justification.assessment: For a polynomial affine in coordinate i, the accepted coordinate-isolation/evaluation identities give p(rho)=a(eta)*rho(i)+b(eta), where eta retains every coordinate other than i and a,b are the actual coordinateSlope and coordinateIntercept polynomials. The domain U consists exactly of eta with eval_eta(a) nonzero, and the root function is exactly -eval_eta(b)/eval_eta(a). No slope oracle or new polynomial model replaces the actual coefficients. The function is total as a Lean real-division expression, but no smoothness or zero-set equivalence is asserted at a zero denominator. A general polynomial may have empty U; the actual central-root application separately proves that its fixed assignment belongs to U, so the source application is not vacuous.

mathematical_justification.clause: Smooth coefficients, rational root and open ambient domain
mathematical_justification.assessment: The pinned multivariate polynomial evaluation theorem is obtained from polynomial induction and analytic coordinate projections, and its global analyticity implies C-infinity smoothness. Applied to the remaining-coordinate slope and intercept polynomials, it proves their evaluations smooth and continuous. The nonzero-slope domain is the complement of the closed equality-to-zero set, hence open. The inspected ContDiffOn division rule uses exactly the nonzero denominator on U and proves the rational root function smooth there. The ambient domain is the preimage of U under the actual remaining-coordinate projection; that projection is continuous, so the ambient domain is open. It allows all values of the moving coordinate, rather than only the original leg or a prespecified graph slice.

The affine specialization theorem identifies evaluation at extendCoordinateAssignment(i,eta,t) with the actual specialized linear polynomial. Its previously proved unique-root equation, under the evaluated nonzero slope, gives zero iff t=-b/a for EVERY real t. Reconstructing an arbitrary actual ambient assignment from its remaining coordinates and its i-th coordinate gives the same iff for every rho in the open ambient domain. To prove the set/image equality, each ambient zero is represented by its own remaining coordinates and reconstructed from that equality. Conversely every graph parameter in U extends to an actual zero, and projecting its unchanged remaining coordinates proves ambient-domain membership. Neither direction omits an actual zero or assumes one is already on the graph.

mathematical_justification.clause: Smooth graph parameterization and smooth projection inverse
mathematical_justification.assessment: The graph map inserts the actual rational root only in coordinate i and retains eta(j) for every other j. Componentwise smoothness follows from the root-function theorem in the i case and actual coordinate projections in the other cases. Applying the remaining-coordinate projection to any graph value recovers eta exactly, so the graph is injective, including for the total graph map outside U. The remaining-coordinate projection is itself globally C-infinity by componentwise smoothness. On the zero set in the ambient domain, the exact root equation reconstructs rho from its projection, giving the other inverse identity; this latter identity was also independently kernel-checked as a separate example. Restricted to U and its graph, these are genuine inverse smooth coordinate maps with their actual induced topologies.

mathematical_justification.clause: Actual central roots supply nonzero slope without an extra premise
mathematical_justification.assessment: The central theorem starts with an actual eval(leg.assignment W r)(namedControlPolynomial name)=0 and the actual JointLegConditions. The exact parameter-polynomial evaluation identity turns this into a genuine parameter root. A control independent of the moving coordinate would remain at a nonzero endpoint value, so the proved root-forces-dependency theorem gives actual variable dependence. JointLegConditions then supplies the evaluated remaining-coordinate slope nonzero. This is precisely membership of leg.fixedAssignment W in U. The assignment_other identity proves that projecting the actual central assignment equals that fixed assignment. The actual root equation therefore places the central i-th coordinate at the root function of those same fixed coordinates. No Generic or Regular centre, root interior, separate gradient assumption, supplied open domain or abstract smoothness premise is used; this valid graph result also covers inactive control roots.

The finite-dimensional scalar ambient space is the actual space of all occurrence scalar coordinates. The parameter domain retains exactly all coordinates except the chosen moving coordinate; the local zero set is the graph of one C-infinity real function over an OPEN subset of that remaining-coordinate space, with smooth inverse projection. This is the explicit smooth-graph characterization of a local embedded hypersurface and gives the substantive source geometry. A separate manifold object or dimension API has not been constructed; it is unnecessary if the source-facing hypersurface predicate uses this explicit characterization. If a later theorem instead asserts a distinct library embedded-submanifold or regular-level predicate, its bridge must be proved rather than inferred from a build. No norm-isometry substitution is required: the smooth statements concern the actual finite scalar-coordinate space.

The independent compiled example assumes only n>=3, an actual leg, W, JointLegConditions and a genuine named-control zero. It internally derives NeZero and the nonzero-slope membership, then assembles the actual open U, smooth injective graph G, smooth remaining projection R, projection-left-inverse identity, open ambient preimage R^{-1}(U), membership of leg.assignment W r in that domain, exhaustive ambient zero-set equality and membership of that actual assignment in G(U). No additional nonzero-slope or smoothness condition is supplied. A second example proves G(R(rho))=rho for every actual ambient zero in the slope neighborhood.
